questions.prompt: How many parts does the Hamburger paragraph have?
questions.explain: It has a Topic Sentence, three Supporting Sentences and a Concluding Sentence.

questions.prompt: Which sentence tells the reader the main idea, or what the paragraph will be about?
questions.explain: The Topic Sentence tells the reader the main idea.

questions.prompt: Which sentence refers to the topic sentence and sums up the main idea of the paragraph?
questions.explain: The Concluding Sentence refers to the topic sentence and sums up the main idea.

questions.prompt: What does a Supporting Sentence give?
choices: Specific details relating to the main idea
A summary of the whole paragraph
questions.answer: Specific details relating to the main idea
questions.explain: Supporting Sentences give specific details relating to the main idea.

questions.prompt: In a Hamburger paragraph, which sentence comes first? (Topic Sentence / Concluding Sentence / Supporting Sentence)
questions.explain: The Topic Sentence is the top bun, so it comes first.

questions.prompt: In a Hamburger paragraph, which sentence comes last? (Topic Sentence / Concluding Sentence / Supporting Sentence)
questions.explain: The Concluding Sentence is the bottom bun, so it comes last.

questions.prompt: How many Supporting Sentences are there in a Hamburger paragraph? Write a number.
questions.explain: There are Supporting Sentences One, Two and Three.

questions.prompt: In the Hamburger paragraph model, which part is the top bun?
questions.explain: The top bun is the Topic Sentence.

questions.prompt: In the Hamburger paragraph model, which part is the bottom bun?
questions.explain: The bottom bun is the Concluding Sentence.

questions.prompt: What does Supporting Sentence Three give?
choices: More specific details relating to the main idea
A summary of the whole paragraph
The main idea of the paragraph
questions.answer: More specific details relating to the main idea
questions.explain: Supporting Sentence Three gives more specific details relating to the main idea.

questions.prompt: The Topic Sentence tells the reader the ___ idea of the paragraph. (one word)
questions.explain: The Topic Sentence tells the reader the main idea.

questions.prompt: The Concluding Sentence refers to the ___ sentence. (one word)
questions.explain: The Concluding Sentence refers to the topic sentence.

questions.prompt: Which list shows the parts of a Hamburger paragraph in the correct order, from top to bottom?
choices: Supporting One, Topic, Supporting Two, Supporting Three, Concluding
Topic, Supporting One, Supporting Two, Supporting Three, Concluding
Topic, Supporting One, Concluding, Supporting Two, Supporting Three
Concluding, Supporting One, Supporting Two, Supporting Three, Topic
questions.answer: Topic, Supporting One, Supporting Two, Supporting Three, Concluding
questions.explain: The order is Topic, three Supporting Sentences, then Concluding.

questions.prompt: Counting from the top bun, what is the third part of the Hamburger paragraph?
questions.explain: The order is Topic, Supporting One, Supporting Two, so the third part is Supporting Sentence Two.

questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT a part of the Hamburger paragraph?
questions.explain: The parts are the Topic, Supporting and Concluding Sentences.

questions.prompt: Which sentence does the reader read right after the Topic Sentence?
questions.explain: Supporting Sentence One comes right after the Topic Sentence.

questions.prompt: Read: (1) Cats make great pets for families. (2) They are quiet, so they do not disturb the neighbours. (3) They also clean themselves, which saves time. (4) For example, a cat can stay alone for a few hours while you are at school. (5) In conclusion, cats are easy and friendly pets. Which sentence number is the Topic Sentence?
questions.explain: Sentence 1 tells the reader what the paragraph is about.

questions.prompt: Read: (1) Cats make great pets for families. (2) They are quiet, so they do not disturb the neighbours. (3) They also clean themselves, which saves time. (4) For example, a cat can stay alone for a few hours while you are at school. (5) In conclusion, cats are easy and friendly pets. Which sentence number is the Concluding Sentence?
questions.explain: Sentence 5 sums up the main idea.

questions.prompt: Read: (1) Cats make great pets for families. (2) They are quiet, so they do not disturb the neighbours. (3) They also clean themselves, which saves time. (4) For example, a cat can stay alone for a few hours while you are at school. (5) In conclusion, cats are easy and friendly pets. What is sentence 4?
questions.explain: Sentences 2, 3 and 4 are Supporting Sentences One, Two and Three.

questions.prompt: Read: (1) Football is a great sport for children. (2) It keeps players fit because they run a lot. (3) It teaches teamwork when players pass the ball. (4) It also helps children make new friends at the club. (5) That is why football is good for young people. Which sentence is the Concluding Sentence?
questions.explain: Sentence 5 sums up the main idea of the paragraph.

questions.prompt: Read: (1) Football is a great sport for children. (2) It keeps players fit because they run a lot. (3) It teaches teamwork when players pass the ball. (4) It also helps children make new friends at the club. (5) That is why football is good for young people. Which sentence number is the Topic Sentence?
questions.explain: Sentence 1 gives the main idea of the paragraph.

questions.prompt: Read: (1) Football is a great sport for children. (2) It keeps players fit because they run a lot. (3) It teaches teamwork when players pass the ball. (4) It also helps children make new friends at the club. (5) That is why football is good for young people. How can you tell that sentence 5 is the Concluding Sentence?
choices: It says what the paragraph will be about
It sums up the main idea of the paragraph
questions.answer: It sums up the main idea of the paragraph
questions.explain: A Concluding Sentence sums up the main idea and refers to the topic sentence.

questions.prompt: Read: (1) Our school library is a wonderful place. (2) It has thousands of books about animals, sport and history. (3) Students can use quiet tables to do their homework. (4) Moreover, the librarian helps us to find a good book. (5) So the library is a very useful place for every student. Which sentence is the Topic Sentence?
questions.explain: Sentence 1 gives the main idea: the library is a wonderful place.

questions.prompt: Read: (1) Our school library is a wonderful place. (2) It has thousands of books about animals, sport and history. (3) Students can use quiet tables to do their homework. (4) Moreover, the librarian helps us to find a good book. (5) So the library is a very useful place for every student. Which sentence is the Concluding Sentence?
questions.explain: Sentence 5 sums up the main idea, so it is the Concluding Sentence.

questions.prompt: Choose the best Topic Sentence for this paragraph. (1) ... (2) Swimming makes our muscles stronger. (3) It also teaches us to stay safe in the water. (4) For example, many children learn to swim at the age of six. (5) In conclusion, swimming is a great sport for children.
choices: Yesterday I went to the pool with my cousin.
Swimming is a very good sport for children.
Pools can be big or small.
questions.answer: Swimming is a very good sport for children.
questions.explain: A good Topic Sentence states the main idea that the details support.

questions.prompt: Choose the best Topic Sentence for this paragraph. (1) ... (2) Fresh vegetables are served every day. (3) The meals are cheap, so every family can pay. (4) The cooks also make vegetarian dishes. (5) To sum up, our canteen offers good food for everyone.
choices: The cooks buy fresh vegetables from a local farm.
Our school canteen serves healthy and cheap meals.
Our canteen is on the first floor.
questions.answer: Our school canteen serves healthy and cheap meals.
questions.explain: The Topic Sentence must give the main idea, not just one detail.

questions.prompt: Choose the best Concluding Sentence for this paragraph. (1) Reading comics is a fun way to practise English. (2) The pictures help you understand new words. (3) Short speech bubbles are easy to read. (4) For instance, many comics repeat useful phrases. (5) ...
choices: My favourite comic is about a dog who lives on a farm.
Comics are sold in many shops around the town.
Some comics have colour pictures on every page.
Comics are an enjoyable way to improve your English.
questions.answer: Comics are an enjoyable way to improve your English.
questions.explain: A Concluding Sentence refers to the topic sentence and sums up the main idea.

questions.prompt: Choose the best Concluding Sentence for this paragraph. (1) Rabbits are easy pets for young children. (2) They eat simple food such as carrots and grass. (3) They do not need long walks. (4) For example, a small garden is enough space for a rabbit. (5) ...
choices: Rabbits are simple and friendly pets for children.
Carrots are orange vegetables that grow in the ground.
Rabbits can jump very high when they are scared.
Dogs are also good pets for families with a garden.
questions.answer: Rabbits are simple and friendly pets for children.
questions.explain: The conclusion sums up the main idea and does not add a new detail or a new topic.

questions.prompt: Read: 'Dogs are nice animals. They are cute. I like dogs. They can run. Some dogs are big, and some are small. Dogs are good.' Is this a strong or a weak Hamburger paragraph? (strong / weak)
questions.explain: It gives very little information, with no details or examples.

questions.prompt: Why is the topic sentence 'Dogs are nice animals' weak?
choices: It has too many linking words.
questions.explain: A weak topic sentence does not explain much.

questions.prompt: What is wrong with the supporting details in the weak paragraph about dogs?
choices: They are too long and too difficult.
They talk about a different topic.
They repeat the Topic Sentence word for word.
The ideas are too simple and lack examples.
questions.answer: The ideas are too simple and lack examples.
questions.explain: Weak supporting details are too simple and lack examples.

questions.prompt: The weak paragraph about dogs ends with 'Dogs are good.' What is the problem with this sentence?
choices: It doesn't summarize the main idea properly.
It is too long to read.
It starts with a linking word.
questions.answer: It doesn't summarize the main idea properly.
questions.explain: A weak conclusion does not summarize the main idea properly.

questions.prompt: Which list shows the three weaknesses of a weak Hamburger paragraph?
choices: Weak title, weak spelling, weak handwriting
Weak topic sentence, weak supporting details, weak conclusion
Weak topic sentence, weak linking words, weak title
Weak supporting details, weak vocabulary, weak conclusion
questions.answer: Weak topic sentence, weak supporting details, weak conclusion
questions.explain: A weak paragraph has a weak topic sentence, weak supporting details and a weak conclusion.

questions.prompt: A strong paragraph explains ideas with details and ___. (one word)
questions.explain: A strong paragraph explains ideas with details and examples.

questions.prompt: A weak paragraph gives very little ___. (one word)
questions.explain: A weak paragraph gives very little information.

questions.prompt: Which description fits a strong paragraph?
choices: It explains ideas with details and examples.
It has only a Topic Sentence.
questions.answer: It explains ideas with details and examples.
questions.explain: A strong paragraph explains ideas with details and examples.

questions.prompt: Which Topic Sentence is weak because it doesn't explain much?
choices: Football is a great sport because it keeps children fit and teaches teamwork.
Football helps children stay healthy, make friends and work as a team.
Playing football every week improves fitness and builds friendships.
questions.explain: A weak topic sentence is too simple and explains little.

questions.prompt: Which Supporting Sentence is the strongest?
choices: For example, running and swimming strengthen our muscles.
questions.answer: For example, running and swimming strengthen our muscles.
questions.explain: A strong supporting sentence gives specific details and examples.

questions.prompt: In the strong paragraph 'Why Exercise Is Important', which sentence is the Topic Sentence?
choices: It improves our fitness, gives us more energy, and helps us feel happier.
Exercise can also reduce stress and help us sleep better at night.
Overall, exercising regularly is an important habit that helps us live healthier and happier lives.
Exercise is one of the best ways to keep our bodies healthy and strong.
questions.answer: Exercise is one of the best ways to keep our bodies healthy and strong.
questions.explain: The first sentence gives the main idea of the paragraph.

questions.prompt: In the strong paragraph 'Why Reading Is Important', what kind of sentence is: 'Reading is an excellent habit that helps people become smarter and more creative.'? (Topic Sentence / Supporting Sentence / Concluding Sentence)
questions.explain: It opens the paragraph and gives the main idea.

questions.prompt: What do linking words do?
choices: They give the title of a paragraph.
questions.explain: Linking words connect sentences and ideas.

questions.prompt: What do linking words help your writing to do?
choices: Become shorter and use fewer words
Flow smoothly and be easier to understand
questions.answer: Flow smoothly and be easier to understand
questions.explain: They help your writing flow smoothly and make paragraphs easier to understand.

questions.prompt: Which job does the linking word 'Furthermore' do?
questions.explain: 'Furthermore' is used for adding ideas.

questions.prompt: Which job does the linking word 'For instance' do?
questions.explain: 'For instance' is used for giving examples.

questions.prompt: Which job does the linking word 'However' do?
questions.explain: 'However' is used for showing contrast.

questions.prompt: Which job does the linking word 'Therefore' do?
questions.explain: 'Therefore' is used for showing results.

questions.prompt: Which job does the linking word 'Firstly' do?
questions.explain: 'Firstly' is used for ordering ideas.

questions.prompt: Which job does the linking word 'In conclusion' do?
questions.explain: 'In conclusion' is used for concluding.

questions.prompt: Which job does the linking word 'Because' do?
questions.explain: 'Because' is used for showing reasons.

questions.prompt: Which job does the linking word 'On the other hand' do?
questions.explain: 'On the other hand' is used for showing contrast.

questions.prompt: Which job does the linking word 'Consequently' do?
questions.explain: 'Consequently' is used for showing results.

questions.prompt: Which job does the linking word 'Finally' do?
questions.explain: 'Finally' is used for ordering ideas.

questions.prompt: The linking word 'moreover' is used for ... (adding ideas / showing contrast / giving examples)
questions.explain: 'Moreover' is used for adding ideas.

questions.prompt: The linking word 'additionally' is used for ... (adding ideas / showing results / concluding)
questions.explain: 'Additionally' is used for adding ideas.

questions.prompt: The linking word 'as a result' is used for ... (showing results / showing contrast / ordering ideas)
questions.explain: 'As a result' is used for showing results.

questions.prompt: The linking word 'secondly' is used for ... (ordering ideas / showing reasons / giving examples)
questions.explain: 'Secondly' is used for ordering ideas.

questions.prompt: The linking word 'next' is used for ... (ordering ideas / showing contrast / concluding)
questions.explain: 'Next' is used for ordering ideas.

questions.prompt: The linking word 'to sum up' is used for ... (concluding / adding ideas / showing contrast)
questions.explain: 'To sum up' is used for concluding.

questions.prompt: The linking word 'for example' is used for ... (giving examples / showing results / ordering ideas)
questions.explain: 'For example' is used for giving examples.

questions.prompt: Which linking word is used for adding ideas?
questions.explain: 'Moreover' adds an idea.

questions.prompt: Which linking word is used for giving examples?
questions.explain: 'For instance' introduces an example.

questions.prompt: Which linking word is used for showing contrast?
questions.explain: 'However' shows contrast.

questions.prompt: Which linking word is used for showing reasons?
questions.explain: 'Because' gives a reason; the other three show results.

questions.prompt: Which linking word is used for showing results?
questions.explain: 'Consequently' shows a result.

questions.prompt: Which linking word is used for ordering ideas?
questions.explain: 'Secondly' orders ideas.

questions.prompt: Which linking word is used for concluding?
questions.explain: 'To sum up' concludes a paragraph.

questions.prompt: Which linking word does NOT belong in the group 'Showing results'?
questions.explain: 'For instance' gives an example; the others show results.

questions.prompt: Which linking word does NOT belong in the group 'Adding ideas'?
questions.explain: 'However' shows contrast; the others add ideas.

questions.prompt: Which linking word does NOT belong in the group 'Ordering ideas'?
questions.explain: 'Therefore' shows a result; the others order ideas.

questions.prompt: Which pair of linking words both show results?
questions.explain: 'Therefore' and 'consequently' both show results.

questions.prompt: Which pair of linking words both give examples?
questions.explain: 'For example' and 'for instance' both give examples.

questions.prompt: Our team lost the match. ___, we trained harder. (As a result / For example / In conclusion)
questions.explain: The training is a result of losing the match.

questions.prompt: I love basketball. ___, my brother prefers tennis.

questions.prompt: Cycling is good for health. ___, it is cheap. (Moreover / For example / In conclusion)
questions.explain: 'Moreover' adds a second advantage.

questions.prompt: Many sports are popular at school. ___, football, tennis and swimming.

questions.prompt: I was late for training ___ the bus was slow. (because / therefore / however)
questions.explain: 'Because' gives the reason.

questions.prompt: The match was cancelled. ___, the players went home.
questions.explain: 'Consequently' shows a result.

questions.prompt: ___, wash your hands. Secondly, take a clean plate. (Firstly / Finally / In conclusion)
questions.explain: 'Firstly' starts an ordered list and 'secondly' follows.

questions.prompt: First we warmed up. Next, we ran. ___, we stretched. (Finally / Firstly / However)
questions.explain: 'Finally' ends a sequence.

questions.prompt: At the end of a paragraph: '___, a good diet helps athletes play well.' (In conclusion / Firstly / However)

questions.prompt: Swimming is fun. ___, the water can be cold. (However / For example / In conclusion)

questions.prompt: Cats sleep a lot during the day. ___, they are very active at night.

questions.prompt: The tickets were sold out. ___, we watched the match at home.

questions.prompt: She studied hard. ___, she passed the exam.

questions.prompt: Which pair of sentences correctly uses a linking word to show a result?
choices: It rained. In conclusion, we stayed inside.
It rained. As a result, we stayed inside.
It rained. For example, we stayed inside.
It rained. Firstly, we stayed inside.
questions.answer: It rained. As a result, we stayed inside.
questions.explain: Staying inside is a result of the rain.

questions.prompt: Which pair of sentences correctly uses a linking word to show contrast?
choices: Maths is difficult. Therefore, I enjoy it.
Maths is difficult. For instance, I enjoy it.
Maths is difficult. However, I enjoy it.
Maths is difficult. To sum up, I enjoy it.
questions.answer: Maths is difficult. However, I enjoy it.
questions.explain: 'However' shows the contrast between difficult and enjoyable.

questions.prompt: Read: 'Basketball is a great sport for students. Firstly, it keeps players fit. Furthermore, it teaches teamwork. However, players can get hurt. In conclusion, basketball is a good choice.' Which linking word shows contrast?
questions.explain: 'However' shows contrast with the earlier ideas.

questions.prompt: Read: 'Basketball is a great sport for students. Firstly, it keeps players fit. Furthermore, it teaches teamwork. However, players can get hurt. In conclusion, basketball is a good choice.' Which linking word adds a second idea?

questions.prompt: Read: 'Basketball is a great sport for students. Firstly, it keeps players fit. Furthermore, it teaches teamwork. However, players can get hurt. In conclusion, basketball is a good choice.' Which linking word starts the Concluding Sentence?
questions.explain: 'In conclusion' opens the Concluding Sentence.

questions.prompt: Read: 'Basketball is a great sport for students. Firstly, it keeps players fit. Furthermore, it teaches teamwork. However, players can get hurt. In conclusion, basketball is a good choice.' Which linking word introduces the first detail?

questions.prompt: Read: 'Cats are easy pets. Firstly, they are quiet. Moreover, they clean themselves. For example, a cat can wash its fur alone. To sum up, cats suit busy families.' Which linking word introduces an example?

questions.prompt: Read: 'Cats are easy pets. Firstly, they are quiet. Moreover, they clean themselves. For example, a cat can wash its fur alone. To sum up, cats suit busy families.' Which linking word adds another advantage?
